172	### ISC Quality System
173	
174	**Every criterion describes one verifiable end-state.** The operational test is granularity:
175	
176	> **Split until each criterion is one binary tool probe.** A criterion is granular enough when a single tool call (`Read`, `Grep`, `Bash`, `curl`, screenshot, `SELECT`, `bun test`, etc.) returns yes/no on whether it's met. If you cannot name the probe, the criterion is not yet atomic — split it. If the criterion needs human judgment, name the tool-verifiable proxy that stands in for the judgment.
177	
178	**Tier floor:** the granularity rule produces a natural N. At E2+, that N must meet the tier ISC floor (E2 ≥16, E3 ≥32, E4 ≥128, E5 ≥256). For complex-app project ISAs, the ISC count naturally runs much higher. E1 has no floor — fast-path stays fast.
179	
180	**Splitting Test** — apply to every criterion as you write it:
181	
182	| Test | Split when... |
183	|------|--------------|
184	| "And"/"With" | Joins two verifiable things |
185	| Independent failure | Part A can pass while B fails |
186	| Scope words | "all", "every", "complete" → enumerate |
187	| Domain boundary | Crosses UI/API/data/logic → one per boundary |
188	| **No nameable probe** | You can't say which tool would verify it |
189	
190	**Format:** `- [ ] ISC-N: criterion text` — the criterion phrasing reveals its category. **All ISCs number sequentially as `ISC-N`** — anti-criteria included. ID-stability rule applies: never re-number on edit; splits become `ISC-N.M`.
191	
192	**Two doctrinal ISC kinds preserved as prose prefix conventions:**
193	
194	| Kind | Surface form | Rule |
195	|------|--------------|------|
196	| **Anti-criterion** — must NOT happen | `- [ ] ISC-N: Anti: <what must NOT happen>` | **≥1 required** |
197	| **Antecedent** — precondition for target experience | `- [ ] ISC-N: Antecedent: <precondition>` | **≥1 required when goal is experiential** |
198	
199	**For complex-app projects: the ISA test surface includes (non-exhaustive):**
200	- **Functional** — features work end-to-end
201	- **API** — endpoints exist, return expected shape, handle errors
202	- **Auth** — sign-in/out, token expiry, magic-link flow, session lifecycle
203	- **Authorization (RBAC/visibility)** — role X can/cannot reach endpoint Y
204	- **Performance** — latency budgets per route, bundle sizes, query times
205	- **Security model** — input validation, output encoding, CSRF, rate limits, secret handling
206	- **Data integrity** — schema invariants, foreign-key consistency, idempotency
207	- **Build & deploy** — `bun build` succeeds, typecheck clean, deploy version matches
208	- **Operational** — `/health` returns 200, error budget within SLO, synthetic monitor up
209	
210	These aren't "in addition to" the ISA — they ARE the ISA. The ISA is the test harness because the ISCs are the tests.
211	
212	**Allowed status markers:**
213	- `- [ ]` — pending, not yet verified
214	- `- [x]` — passed, verified with evidence
215	- `- [DEFERRED-VERIFY]` — passed in code/intent but live probe is impossible at execution time. **Requires a follow-up task ID in the verification notes.** Cannot be marked `[x]` until the deferred probe runs.

# Interceptor — Stealth Browser Automation

**Tool:** `interceptor` CLI — Chrome extension that controls the real browser from the inside.
**Repo:** https://github.com/Hacker-Valley-Media/slop-browser
**Install:** `~/Projects/interceptor` (built from source — see `Workflows/Update.md`)

### Why Interceptor?

agent-browser (the Browser skill) uses CDP — sites can detect it. Interceptor is a Chrome extension that operates through the actual browser UI. No debugger, no automation flags, no separate browser instance. You stay logged in, you pass bot detection, the agent sees what you see.

### Prerequisites

- Chrome or Brave running with the Interceptor extension loaded
- `interceptor` CLI in PATH (`/opt/homebrew/bin/interceptor`)
- `interceptor-daemon` in PATH (`/opt/homebrew/bin/interceptor-daemon`)
- Native messaging manifest registered (`bash ~/Projects/interceptor/scripts/install.sh --chrome --skip-extension`)
- (Optional, macOS) `interceptor-bridge` helper app — see "Bridge" section below

### Remote Execution — Linux box → Mac over SSH (REQUIRED on the Linux host)

Interceptor is a Chrome extension; it only runs where a real, logged-in Chrome
is. The Linux workstation has **no Chrome and no interceptor binary** — do not
try to install or run it locally there. Instead, drive the interceptor that
already lives on the Mac (where Nick stays logged into Seek, LinkedIn, etc.)
over SSH. The Mac is reachable as the `mac` / `nicholass-macbook-pro` SSH alias.

Prefix every interceptor command with the SSH hop and the Homebrew PATH (the
non-interactive SSH shell does not inherit `/opt/homebrew/bin`):

```bash
# Preflight: confirm the Mac, daemon, and Chrome are all up
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor status; pgrep -lf "Google Chrome" | head -1'

# Any interceptor command, run on the Mac's real browser:
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor open "https://www.seek.com.au/my-activity/saved-jobs" --text-only'
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor scroll bottom; interceptor wait 1500; interceptor text | tail -90'
```

Wrap long output in `| head`/`| tail` to keep it bounded. Use `timeout 90 ssh …`
so a hung page can't stall the turn. Everything else in this skill works
unchanged once you've prefixed the SSH hop — refs, compound commands, network
log, scene graph all behave identically; they just execute on the Mac.

### Bridge — macOS Native Helper App

The bridge is an optional Swift helper that runs as a LaunchAgent and unlocks
capabilities the Chrome extension can't provide on its own: OS-level synthetic
input (`act --os`), accessibility tree of native macOS apps, app control,
clipboard, screen capture beyond Chrome, audio/speech, files, notifications,
HealthKit, Apple Intelligence. ~95% of typical work doesn't need it.

**Status check:** `interceptor status` reports `bridge: running` with PID + socket
when it's up, or `bridge: not running` when it isn't.

**Lifecycle (install / verify / troubleshoot / uninstall) lives entirely in
`Workflows/Update.md` section 6.** Future updates flow through the Update
workflow — never reach for the upstream `install-bridge.sh` directly; that
script breaks on Apple Silicon (`/usr/local/bin` needs sudo, but sudoing the
whole script makes `launchctl bootstrap` target uid 0 instead of the user).
The skill's procedure is the canonical one.

**Security model — read before installing:**

- Transport is a **UNIX domain socket** at `/tmp/interceptor-bridge.sock`.
  Local-only; no network listener; not reachable from another machine.
- **No authentication on the socket.** Any local process running as your user
  can connect and execute every bridge action — including synthetic input,
  clipboard read, audio capture, screenshots. macOS TCC permissions
  (Accessibility, Input Monitoring, Screen Recording, Microphone) are granted
  to the bridge once and inherited by every socket client.
- **Marginal risk is supply-chain:** a malicious package installed via
  bun/brew/npm gains a one-step path to OS-level input/screen/clipboard without
  needing its own permission grants — the bridge has them.
- Single-user Mac threat model: acceptable, since anything running as you can
  already do this with effort. Multi-user Macs need socket hardening (see
  Update.md section 6c).
- Binary built locally from `~/Projects/interceptor/interceptor-bridge/Sources/`,
  not a downloaded prebuilt. Provenance is Swift source we just compiled.

## Compound Commands (Preferred)

These collapse multi-step patterns into single invocations — fewer tool calls, fewer tokens:

```bash
interceptor open "https://example.com"              # Open URL, wait, return tree + text
interceptor open <url> --tree-only|--text-only|--full|--no-wait
interceptor read                                     # Tree + text for active tab
interceptor read <ref>                               # Tree + text for element subtree
interceptor read --include-style|--include-frames
interceptor act <ref>                                # Click + wait + return updated tree + diff
interceptor act <ref> "value"                        # Type + wait + return updated tree
interceptor act <ref> --os                           # OS-level trusted input (requires bridge)
interceptor act <ref> --keys "Enter"                 # Send keyboard shortcut
interceptor inspect                                  # Tree + text + network log + headers
interceptor inspect --net-only                       # Network only
```

## Core Commands

```bash
# State + discovery
interceptor state [--full]              # DOM tree + metadata
interceptor tree [--filter all] [--depth N] [--max-chars N]
interceptor diff                         # Changes since last state/tree read
interceptor find "query" [--role button] # Find elements by name
interceptor text [<index|ref>]
interceptor html <index|ref>

# Element interaction
interceptor click <ref>                  # Click by ref (eN)
interceptor click <ref> --at X,Y         # Click at coordinates
interceptor dblclick <ref> --at X,Y
interceptor rightclick <ref> --at X,Y
interceptor type <ref> <text> [--append]
interceptor type "role:name" <text>      # Semantic selector
interceptor select <ref> <value>         # Dropdown
interceptor focus|hover <ref>
interceptor drag <ref> --from X,Y --to X,Y [--steps N] [--duration MS]
interceptor keys "<combo>"               # e.g. "Control+A"

# Navigation + tabs
interceptor navigate <url>
interceptor back | forward
interceptor scroll <up|down|top|bottom>
interceptor wait <ms> | wait-stable [--ms N] [--timeout N]
interceptor tabs
interceptor tab new [url] | tab close [id] | tab switch <id>

# Capture
interceptor screenshot [--save] [--format png|jpeg] [--full] [--clip X,Y,W,H] [--element N]
interceptor eval <code> [--main]         # JS in isolated or main world
interceptor capture start | frame | stop # tabCapture stream

# Style injection (test redesigns live)
interceptor style inject --css "<rules>" [--top-only]
interceptor style remove <handle>

# Cookies
interceptor cookies <domain>
interceptor cookies set <json>
interceptor cookies delete <url> <name>
```

## Network

```bash
# Passive capture (always-on, no CDP fingerprint)
interceptor net log [--filter <pat>] [--limit N] [--since <ts>]
interceptor net headers [--filter <pat>]   # CSRF, auth headers
interceptor net clear

# Request override (passive, no CDP)
interceptor override "*pattern*" key=value
interceptor override clear

# CDP-attached interception (explicit opt-in — leaves debugger banner)
interceptor network on [patterns...]
interceptor network off
interceptor network log
interceptor network override on '<json>'
interceptor network override off

# SSE streams (LLM responses, live feeds)
interceptor sse log [--filter <pat>] [--limit N]
interceptor sse streams
interceptor sse tail [--filter <pat>]

# Header rewriting
interceptor headers add <name> <value>
interceptor headers remove <name>
interceptor headers clear
```

## Recording (Session Monitor)

Record real user actions on the active tab, replay as a deterministic plan script.

```bash
interceptor monitor start ["instruction"]   # Start recording
interceptor monitor pause | resume
interceptor monitor stop                     # End + emit summary
interceptor monitor status [--all]
interceptor monitor list                     # All sessions
interceptor monitor tail [--current] [--raw] # Live tail
interceptor monitor export <sessionId>       # Aligned text
interceptor monitor export <sessionId> --plan # Replay script
interceptor monitor export <sessionId> --json
```

## Canvas (Rich Web Apps)

For apps that render to `<canvas>` (Figma, Excalidraw, in-house editors):

```bash
interceptor canvas list | status
interceptor canvas log [N] [--kind fillText]
interceptor canvas objects [N] [--kind text]
interceptor canvas model | routes
interceptor canvas ocr N [--region X,Y,W,H]
interceptor canvas read N [--format png] [--region X,Y,W,H] [--webgl]
interceptor canvas diff <url1> <url2> [--threshold 10] [--image]
```

## Scene Graph (Rich Editors — Google Docs/Slides, Canva)

```bash
interceptor scene profile [--verbose]
interceptor scene list [--type shape|text|image|page|embed|slide]
interceptor scene click <id> | dblclick <id> | select <id>
interceptor scene hit <x> <y>                # ID object at coordinates
interceptor scene selected | text [--with-html]
interceptor scene insert "<text>"
interceptor scene cursor-to <x> <y>
interceptor scene slide list | current | goto <index> | notes [--slide N]
interceptor scene render <id> [--save]
interceptor scene zoom
interceptor scene ... --profile <name>       # Force profile, bypass detection
```

## LinkedIn

```bash
interceptor linkedin event [url]             # Event + post data via DOM + network
interceptor linkedin attendees [url]         # Attendees with override + enrichment
```

## ChatGPT Agentic Bridge

Drive chatgpt.com from CLI without an API key:

```bash
interceptor chatgpt send "<prompt>" [--stream]
interceptor chatgpt read | status
interceptor chatgpt conversations | switch <id>
interceptor chatgpt model [name]
interceptor chatgpt stop
```

## Batch + Meta

```bash
interceptor batch '<json_array>' [--stop-on-error] [--timeout MS]
interceptor status                    # Daemon + bridge state (local check)
interceptor help
```

## Key Rules

- **Requires Chrome running** — it's an extension, not a standalone binary.
- **Refs use eN syntax** — `e12` not `@e12`. No `@` prefix.
- **Cross-frame refs** — `read --include-frames` returns refs like `e<frameId>_<n>` for non-top frames.
- **`--json`** is a global flag for structured output.
- **Daemon auto-starts** — first command launches it; no manual start needed.
- **Bridge is optional** — only needed for `act --os` and OS-trusted input. Without it, interceptor falls back to in-page synthetic events.

## Delegating to Agents

When spawning agents for Interceptor work:

```
Agent(subagent_type="general-purpose", prompt="
  Use interceptor CLI for all browser work.
  Commands: open <url>, read, act eN, act eN 'text', inspect, screenshot.
  Compound commands preferred — they return tree + text in one call.
  Refs use eN syntax (no @ prefix) from tree output.
  Use --json for structured output.
  [your specific task instructions here]
")
```

## Gotchas

- **Screenshot ignores scroll position.** `interceptor screenshot` (with or without `--full`) captures from y=0 of the document — it does not honor `window.scrollTo`, `scrollIntoView`, `scroll bottom`, or `keys End`. For tall pages, content below the fold is unreachable through screenshot. Workaround: render the section of interest at its own short URL (`/problems.html`, `/section-3.html`) and screenshot that page directly. The `--clip "x,y,w,h"` flag returns "Cannot read properties of undefined" — broken in the current build. *(2026-04-27)*
- **Multiple tabs at the same URL confuse routing.** When two tabs both load `localhost:5180/`, `tab switch <id>` reports `ok` but the visually-active Chrome tab may not change, and `screenshot` captures whatever Chrome is showing — not what `interceptor text` and `interceptor navigate` are routing to. Close duplicate tabs before screenshotting, or always work from a freshly-opened single tab.
- **`eval` is CSP-blocked on most sites.** Use `eval --main` to run in the page's main world instead of the isolated extension world. Even with `--main`, sites with strict CSP (`script-src 'self'`) will still block string-eval; pass small expressions only and avoid `Function`-constructor patterns.
- **MV3 service worker idles in seconds — wake it and act in ONE SSH session.** "error: no extensions connected" usually means the extension's service worker went idle, not that the install broke. Wake it by opening a window in its profile (`open -na "Google Chrome" --args --profile-directory="Profile 3"`), sleep ~5s, then chain ALL interceptor commands in the same SSH invocation — a follow-up `ssh` call ~10s later will find the worker asleep again. *(2026-08-23)*
- **No Chrome / no binary on the Linux box — run on the Mac over SSH.** `which interceptor` returns nothing on the Linux workstation and there is no Chrome/Brave/Chromium installed there, so the skill appears "broken" if you try to run it locally. It is not broken — it lives on the Mac. Hop to it: `ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor <cmd>'`. The `export PATH` is mandatory (non-interactive SSH shells miss `/opt/homebrew/bin`). See "Remote Execution" under Prerequisites. *(2026-06-16)*

## Stealth Verification

Passes all major bot detection:

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| BrowserScan | Normal |
| Pixelscan | Definitely Human |
| Sannysoft | All pass |
| CreepJS | 0% headless |
| Fingerprint.com | notDetected |
| AreyouHeadless | Not headless |

---

## Workflow Routing

| Trigger Words | Workflow | What It Does |
|--------------|----------|-------------|
| "verify deploy", "check deploy", "confirm deploy", "deploy verification" | `Workflows/VerifyDeploy.md` | Open URL in real Chrome, check for errors, capture screenshot evidence |
| "reproduce", "reproduce bug", "debug page", "check page", "blank screen" | `Workflows/Reproduce.md` | Open affected page BEFORE code analysis, capture console errors and network 404s |
| "record flow", "record workflow", "capture flow", "monitor start" | `Workflows/RecordFlow.md` | Record user actions via monitor system, export replayable plan script |
| "replay flow", "replay", "regression check", "run flow" | `Workflows/ReplayFlow.md` | Execute a recorded plan script step-by-step, verify each step, report regressions |
| "test form", "fill form", "form test", "check form" | `Workflows/TestForm.md` | Discover form fields, fill with test data, submit, verify result |
| "update", "check version", "rebuild" | `Workflows/Update.md` | Rebuild interceptor from source and verify |

---

## Execution Log

After completing any workflow, append a single JSONL entry:

```bash
echo '{"ts":"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'","skill":"Interceptor","workflow":"WORKFLOW_USED","input":"8_WORD_SUMMARY","status":"ok|error","duration_s":SECONDS}' >> ~/.claude/PAI/MEMORY/SKILLS/execution.jsonl
```

## Key Rules

- **Requires Chrome running** — it's an extension, not a standalone binary.
- **Refs use eN syntax** — `e12` not `@e12`. No `@` prefix.
- **Cross-frame refs** — `read --include-frames` returns refs like `e<frameId>_<n>` for non-top frames.
- **`--json`** is a global flag for structured output.
- **Daemon auto-starts** — first command launches it; no manual start needed.
- **Bridge is optional** — only needed for `act --os` and OS-trusted input. Without it, interceptor falls back to in-page synthetic events.

## Delegating to Agents

When spawning agents for Interceptor work:

```
Agent(subagent_type="general-purpose", prompt="
  Use interceptor CLI for all browser work.
  Commands: open <url>, read, act eN, act eN 'text', inspect, screenshot.
  Compound commands preferred — they return tree + text in one call.
  Refs use eN syntax (no @ prefix) from tree output.
  Use --json for structured output.
  [your specific task instructions here]
")
```

## Gotchas

- **Screenshot ignores scroll position.** `interceptor screenshot` (with or without `--full`) captures from y=0 of the document — it does not honor `window.scrollTo`, `scrollIntoView`, `scroll bottom`, or `keys End`. For tall pages, content below the fold is unreachable through screenshot. Workaround: render the section of interest at its own short URL (`/problems.html`, `/section-3.html`) and screenshot that page directly. The `--clip "x,y,w,h"` flag returns "Cannot read properties of undefined" — broken in the current build. *(2026-04-27)*
- **Multiple tabs at the same URL confuse routing.** When two tabs both load `localhost:5180/`, `tab switch <id>` reports `ok` but the visually-active Chrome tab may not change, and `screenshot` captures whatever Chrome is showing — not what `interceptor text` and `interceptor navigate` are routing to. Close duplicate tabs before screenshotting, or always work from a freshly-opened single tab.
- **`eval` is CSP-blocked on most sites.** Use `eval --main` to run in the page's main world instead of the isolated extension world. Even with `--main`, sites with strict CSP (`script-src 'self'`) will still block string-eval; pass small expressions only and avoid `Function`-constructor patterns.
- **MV3 service worker idles in seconds — wake it and act in ONE SSH session.** "error: no extensions connected" usually means the extension's service worker went idle, not that the install broke. Wake it by opening a window in its profile (`open -na "Google Chrome" --args --profile-directory="Profile 3"`), sleep ~5s, then chain ALL interceptor commands in the same SSH invocation — a follow-up `ssh` call ~10s later will find the worker asleep again. *(2026-08-23)*
- **No Chrome / no binary on the Linux box — run on the Mac over SSH.** `which interceptor` returns nothing on the Linux workstation and there is no Chrome/Brave/Chromium installed there, so the skill appears "broken" if you try to run it locally. It is not broken — it lives on the Mac. Hop to it: `ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor <cmd>'`. The `export PATH` is mandatory (non-interactive SSH shells miss `/opt/homebrew/bin`). See "Remote Execution" under Prerequisites. *(2026-06-16)*

#!/bin/bash
# Opens the Cloud SQL public-IP window and runs cloud-sql-proxy on 127.0.0.1:5433
# so the reactivation backfill can be run from the Linux box over an SSH tunnel.
# Writes the proxy-local DATABASE_URL to ~/pai-tmp/.dburl (mode 600) and never
# prints it. Closes the window when ~/pai-tmp/rx-close appears or after 20 min,
# then verifies ipv4Enabled is False.
set -u
G=/opt/homebrew/bin/gcloud
P=/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/bin/psql
PROXY=/opt/homebrew/bin/cloud-sql-proxy
PROJECT=accessbuddy-prod
INST=accessbuddy-production
REGION=australia-southeast1
FLAG="$HOME/pai-tmp/rx-close"
PROXY_PID=""
rm -f "$FLAG"

cleanup() {
  [ -n "$PROXY_PID" ] && kill "$PROXY_PID" 2>/dev/null
  rm -f "$HOME/pai-tmp/.dburl"
  $G sql instances patch $INST --project $PROJECT --no-assign-ip --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1
  echo "IPV4_ENABLED_AFTER=$($G sql instances describe $INST --project $PROJECT --format='value(settings.ipConfiguration.ipv4Enabled)')"
  echo "CLOSED_AT=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

DBURL=$($G run services describe accessbuddy-production --region $REGION --project $PROJECT --format=json 2>/dev/null \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; env=json.load(sys.stdin)['spec']['template']['spec']['containers'][0]['env']; print([e['value'] for e in env if e['name']=='DATABASE_URL'][0])")
if [ -z "$DBURL" ]; then echo "NO_DBURL"; exit 1; fi
LOCALURL=$(printf '%s' "$DBURL" | sed -E 's#@[^/@]+/#@127.0.0.1:5433/#')
umask 077
printf '%s' "$LOCALURL" > "$HOME/pai-tmp/.dburl"

echo "== opening IP window $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
$G sql instances patch $INST --project $PROJECT --assign-ip --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "PATCH_FAILED"; exit 1; }
$PROXY --port 5433 "$PROJECT:$REGION:$INST" >"$HOME/pai-tmp/proxy.log" 2>&1 &
PROXY_PID=$!
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if $P "$LOCALURL" -Atc "select 1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "DB_CONNECTED after ${i}s"; break; fi
  sleep 1
done
echo "READY"

for i in $(seq 1 1200); do
  [ -f "$FLAG" ] && { echo "close flag seen"; break; }
  sleep 1
done

#!/bin/bash
# Opens the Cloud SQL public-IP window and runs cloud-sql-proxy on 127.0.0.1:5433
# so the reactivation backfill can be run from the Linux box over an SSH tunnel.
# Writes the proxy-local DATABASE_URL to ~/pai-tmp/.dburl (mode 600) and never
# prints it. Closes the window when ~/pai-tmp/rx-close appears or after 20 min,
# then verifies ipv4Enabled is False.
set -u
G=/opt/homebrew/bin/gcloud
P=/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/bin/psql
PROXY=/opt/homebrew/bin/cloud-sql-proxy
PROJECT=accessbuddy-prod
INST=accessbuddy-production
REGION=australia-southeast1
FLAG="$HOME/pai-tmp/rx-close"
PROXY_PID=""
rm -f "$FLAG"

cleanup() {
  [ -n "$PROXY_PID" ] && kill "$PROXY_PID" 2>/dev/null
  rm -f "$HOME/pai-tmp/.dburl"
  $G sql instances patch $INST --project $PROJECT --no-assign-ip --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1
  echo "IPV4_ENABLED_AFTER=$($G sql instances describe $INST --project $PROJECT --format='value(settings.ipConfiguration.ipv4Enabled)')"
  echo "CLOSED_AT=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

DBURL=$($G run services describe accessbuddy-production --region $REGION --project $PROJECT --format=json 2>/dev/null \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; env=json.load(sys.stdin)['spec']['template']['spec']['containers'][0]['env']; print([e['value'] for e in env if e['name']=='DATABASE_URL'][0])")
if [ -z "$DBURL" ]; then echo "NO_DBURL"; exit 1; fi
LOCALURL=$(printf '%s' "$DBURL" | sed -E 's#@[^/@]+/#@127.0.0.1:5433/#')
umask 077
printf '%s' "$LOCALURL" > "$HOME/pai-tmp/.dburl"

echo "== opening IP window $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
$G sql instances patch $INST --project $PROJECT --assign-ip --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "PATCH_FAILED"; exit 1; }
$PROXY --port 5433 "$PROJECT:$REGION:$INST" >"$HOME/pai-tmp/proxy.log" 2>&1 &
PROXY_PID=$!
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if $P "$LOCALURL" -Atc "select 1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "DB_CONNECTED after ${i}s"; break; fi
  sleep 1
done
echo "READY"

for i in $(seq 1 1200); do
  [ -f "$FLAG" ] && { echo "close flag seen"; break; }
  sleep 1
done

## Decisions

- 2026-11-22: Nick: "check why Helen Osman's attestation is showing up twice in the list? She only has one fob." Diagnosis only, no code or data changed. The admin dashboard lists one row per pending `attestation_requests` record (no join fan-out; fob count is irrelevant), and nothing stops a second pending renewal row for the same member and season: `POST /members/[id]/renew` always inserts, the member page Re-send (`attestation-section.tsx` `handleResend`) re-sends by calling Renew again, and the Renew button allows a second click. The member page shows only one pending renewal (`pendings.find`), so the extra row is visible on the dashboard only. Production request log (30 days): three members got two 200 Renew calls 4 to 6 s apart (11, 15, 18 Nov); cron on a 7-day cycle heals a same-day pair to one row at lapse. Not verified: which of Helen's rows exist (logs carry no names, Interceptor extension would not connect, prod DB window not opened from a background job). A scoped fob confirmation alongside a renewal is the other possible cause and renders identically on the dashboard. Proposed, not built: Renew reuses a live pending renewal row (rotate token, re-send) instead of inserting; partial unique index on pending non-scoped (tenant, user, season); completing one row closes siblings; dashboard row labels fob confirmations.

- 2026-11-16: Lockers module (ISC-204..266). Nick: "I would like to add the locker code into AccessBuddy. There should be a feature flag per tenancy, set at the global admin level ... and a separate set of permissions to approve lockers and update lockers." Source: legacy Apps Script `lifesaving/smlsc/club-renewal/artifacts/legacy-lockers/lockers/` (byte-identical to the 16 Nov export) and "SMLSC Locker Request (Responses).xlsx". Confirmed by Nick 16 Nov: approve and allocate are one step; revoke sits under Approve lockers; lockers are requested through the same public form as fobs (details entered once) with its own QR; a locker shows on the member profile like a credential; no hard per-member limit (approver warned); from next season the confirmation asks members whether they keep their locker; a club-set cutoff date (SMLSC: 1 December) releases lockers of unrenewed members to the Update lockers holders for clean-out and label clearing; import the SMLSC data; fix the cross-tenant role join as its own PR. Design review (advisor) added: guarded state changes against double approval, a seven-day clean-out hold before a locker is re-suggested, cutoff arming so a newly saved cutoff cannot mass-release for a season whose date has passed, cascade from a rejected fob request to its locker request, signed-out submissions never bound to a member account. Not adopted: changing `sendAdminNotification` recipients; ending allocations on member archive. Delegation: accessbuddy-feature-dev (backend, then UI), accessbuddy-qa-verify gate. Cato skipped: codex CLI absent on the Linux box.

- 2026-10-23: Nick, after cancelling the mis-staged request: "I then also had to separately cancel the programming. That is done but adding the fob back is still blocked." Request log: cancel 200 → add 400 → cancel-programming 200 → add 400. Cause by code: the CANCEL branch flags any non-deactivated linked credential for deactivation regardless of whether it was ever programmed (the comment says "programmed" but the code never checked), so a `pending_programming` manual add got a phantom deactivation flag; and the expiry-update stage's eligible statuses omitted `pending_programming`, so once the flag was cleared the fob was refused as "pending programming". Fix PR on `fix/readd-pending-programming-fob` (ISC-174..176): never-programmed cancels only unallocate; `pending_programming` is eligible when unowned or already on this member, refused when pending for someone else. Both covered by DB-gated tests. Pre-existing bug in cancel, not introduced by #111/#117.

- 2026-10-19: Nick after the v1.23.0 deploy: "I just added the fob and it went straight to programming, not waiting for member to confirm". Reproduction by production request log (the Mac, and so Interceptor and the DB, dropped off the network repeatedly): one `POST /api/v1/t/south-melb-lsc/credentials` at 09:39:24Z → 201, no attest-link or renew call around it, and the refreshed member page immediately prefetched a brand-new request id, which only the three original stages create. Deployed main checked: the expiry-update branch returns before the tracking-request insert and never flags programming. Cause: the form preselected "Send for Programming" and a deactivated/unassigned fob is offered under every stage, so fob-then-button ran the old path. Fix on `fix/add-credential-explicit-stage`: no preselected stage (button disabled until chosen) and a fob whose record still points at this member auto-selects the expiry-update stage. Not a server defect; no server change. Tidy-up for the live fob: cancel the created request and re-add with the expiry-update stage. Lesson for the ISA: a form default is part of the flow's correctness; ISC-158 should have pinned "no stage preselected" when the fourth option was added.

📃 CONTENT:

**Helen's duplicate is almost certainly two pending attestation records, not one record shown twice. I could not see her actual rows, so which of two causes applies is still unconfirmed.**

The Requests page lists one row per pending attestation record and has nothing to do with how many fobs a member holds. Nothing in AccessBuddy stops a member having two pending records for the same season.

**How a second record gets created**
- **Renew always inserts.** The Renew route creates a new pending attestation every time it is called and never checks for an existing one.
- **Re-send on the member page is Renew in disguise.** Its Re-send button calls Renew again, so it adds a second record and sends a second email with a different link.
- **The member page hides it.** The Confirmations card shows only one pending renewal, so the extra record is visible on the Requests page only.

**What production shows**
- Three members received two successful Renew calls 4 to 6 seconds apart, on 11, 15 and 18 November.
- The 15 and 18 November members each have two pending rows on the dashboard today.
- None of those three was found by searching for Helen (the admin's search terms were "porter", "Silvy" and "shac"), so I cannot say she is one of them.
- Tokens last 7 days. A same-day pair collapses to one row when both lapse, because the nightly job re-sends one fresh attestation per member and season.

**The other possible cause:** a fob confirmation (from re-adding a fob she already holds) sitting alongside a normal renewal. The two look identical on the Requests page, which shows only name, season and token expiry.

**How to tell which, in ten seconds:** compare the "token expires" dates on Helen's two rows.
- Same date: a double Renew.
- Different dates: either a Re-send or Renew on a later day, or a fob confirmation plus a renewal. Her member page's Confirmations card will show a separate "Fob confirmation" entry in the second case.

**Why I could not confirm it myself**
- Request logs carry no names or emails.
- The Interceptor extension on the Mac would not connect. I opened two extra Chrome windows in Profile 3 trying to wake it; they are safe to close.
- I did not open the production database window from a background job.

**One side effect to know about:** if Helen completes one link, the other record stays pending and keeps showing until it lapses. Depending on which record is newer, the nightly job can then email her a fresh attestation she has already completed.

**What I changed:** nothing in code or production data. I added one entry to the Decisions log in the AccessBuddy `ISA.md`.

**Fix I would recommend (not built):**
1. Make Renew reuse a live pending renewal (new link, re-send) instead of inserting.
2. Add a database uniqueness rule for pending renewals per member and season.
3. Close sibling records when one is completed.
4. Label fob confirmations on the Requests page.

- Traced the list query, every insert path, production logs.
- Renew and Re-send both create duplicate pending records.
- Her specific rows still need one look to confirm.

cat > /home/nicholas-wood/.claude/jobs/6fff0ac7/tmp/pr-body.md <<'EOF'
## Why

A member could appear twice under Attestation Pending on the Requests page. Renew inserted a new pending attestation on every call, and the member page Re-send worked by calling Renew, so a repeated click or a re-send left two pending records and two live links. The member page only ever showed one of them.

Production request log, last 30 days: three members received two successful Renew calls 4 to 6 seconds apart (11, 15 and 18 November).

## What changed

- **Renew** re-issues the link on the member's existing pending renewal instead of inserting. A repeat inside 60 seconds is treated as a repeated click: no second email, no new link, no second audit line. The membership row is locked so concurrent calls queue.
- **Migration 0022** closes existing duplicates (newest kept, older marked `expired`) and adds a partial unique index on pending non-scoped `(tenant_id, user_id, season)`.
- **Member page Re-send** uses `resend-attestation` on the pending row.
- **Renew button** reloads the page and shows a notice, so the result of the click is visible.
- **Nightly auto-resend** never adds a renewal while one is pending.
- **Requests page** names a fob confirmation ("Fob confirmation pending for Fob #123") so it is not mistaken for a second renewal attestation.

## Things to know before merging

- The migration marks the older row of each existing duplicate pair `expired`. A member holding both emails must use the most recent one; the older link will say it has expired.
- A Re-send from the member page now writes the `attestation_resent` audit line rather than `renew`.
- Scoped fob confirmations are not covered by the index. They are already limited to one pending row per fob in the Add Credential route.

## Verification

- Typecheck clean, lint 0 errors.
- Full suite against Postgres: 1,265 passed, 0 skipped (web 1,196 including 7 new in `renew-single-pending-attestation.test.ts`).
- Migration run against a seeded fixture: of three duplicate pending renewals the newest stayed pending and two became `expired`; scoped, other-season, completed and single rows untouched; index created; no duplicate groups left.
- `lockers-season.test.ts`: one fixture created three pending attestations for the same member in a loop; it now clears each before the next.

Not yet done: a browser pass on the live site after release.
EOF

**The fix is built and waiting for your merge: [PR #139](https://github.com/nicholas-wood/accessbuddy/pull/139), CI green.** Nothing is deployed yet and no production data has been touched.

**What it changes**
- **Renew** now re-issues the link on the member's existing pending renewal instead of creating a second one. A repeat within 60 seconds is treated as a double-click and sends no second email.
- **Database rule:** one pending renewal per member per season. The migration first closes existing duplicates, keeping the newest and marking older ones expired.
- **Member page Re-send** now re-sends the existing attestation in place.
- **Renew button** reloads the page and shows a notice, so the click visibly did something.
- **Nightly re-send job** never adds a renewal while one is pending.
- **Requests page** names fob confirmations ("Fob confirmation pending for Fob #123") so they are not mistaken for a second renewal.

**How it was checked**
- All 1,265 tests pass against a real Postgres with none skipped, including seven new ones.
- I ran the migration against a seeded set of duplicates: it kept the newest, expired the older two, and left fob confirmations, other seasons and completed rows alone.
- One existing locker test created three pending attestations for the same member in a loop, which the new rule forbids. I changed it to clear each one first.
- The "Claude Code Review" check passed in 18 seconds, which is too fast to be a real review. Treat this change as unreviewed.

- When the migration runs, any member currently holding two emails (the 15 and 18 November pairs, and Helen if she is one) must use the newer link. The older one will say it has expired.
- A Re-send from the member page will now appear in the audit trail as "attestation resent" rather than "renew".
- I dropped "completing one closes its siblings" from the earlier list, because the database rule makes siblings impossible.

**Still owed**
- A browser pass on the live Requests page and a member page after release. Interceptor would not connect this session.
- Confirming Helen shows once. I never saw her actual rows, so that is the real proof.
